brief: Opt-in MTP speculative decoding for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B using the checkpoint's MTP head; greedy output must stay token-identical to MTP off; design GatedDeltaNet rollback explicitly; reuse the n-gram verify path.
hypothesis: vLLM/SGLang report large decode gains from Qwen3.x MTP heads; a k+1-row verify pass reads the weights once, so with high acceptance decode tok/s should rise well above plain decode on GB10 without changing greedy output.

summary: --spec mtp works opt-in on CUDA with greedy output token-identical to off and verify rows bitwise equal to M=1 decode. In a quiet localeval slot k=2 gives +2.4% / +4.8% / +9.0% at 128 / 1k / 4k (acceptance 62.8%, 2.25 tokens/pass): a tie at 128 and 1k, a small win at 4k. Code/arithmetic prompts with 70-93% acceptance gained 16-33% in a shared slot. The verify pass costs ~25 ms vs 11.6 ms per plain step, so break-even is ~2.16 tokens/pass. vLLM's MTP (101.4 tok/s at 1k) stays ahead in the spec cell. At the start the lane's 1k spec-cell entry was plain decode, 84.6 tok/s vs vLLM NVFP4 MTP 101.4 (regimes.json built 00:19, same_quant_margin_pct null), -16.6% by this lane's arithmetic; after k=2 87.8 vs 101.4, -13.4%.
lessons: On GB10 the eager verify pass (~14 ms fixed + ~5 ms per row) is the limit, not acceptance; graph-capture it before tuning k.
localeval speed prompts accept far less than code/arithmetic prompts (62.8% vs 70-93% at k=2); quote MTP gains with the acceptance they came from.
Bitwise verify rows are a property of the current CUDA small-M kernel selection (GEMV at q<=3), measured, not enforced; mark those kernels rows_exact before relying on it.
A plan dry-run that skips the drafter head lets the server load and then fail on the first spec pass (#4371); dry-run every graph the request can execute.
decode_tps measurements are medians of 3 interleaved passes per arm; before/after_run_id name the p2 passes, all run ids are in the results doc section 3.2.
